findings.claim: source_mutated's undo (`git checkout HEAD -- <file>`) is justified by the docstring's claim (lines 393-395) that `committed` guarantees the agent's work is already committed before any gate runs, so HEAD is what the file should return to. That guarantee does not hold at this point: in saffron/cell/session.py, `committed_gate` (line 1049) is computed strictly after `declared = run_suite(...)` (line 1008, which invokes this mutator), and no unconditional host-side commit happens between a normal IMPLEMENT/REPAIR turn finishing and `_run_gates` being called (session.py's host checkpoint-commit only fires on the AgentFailed exception path, e.g. lines 1451-1455 and 1573-1576). If a criterion's mutant targets a file the agent has genuinely left uncommitted at that point, applying the mutant and then checking out HEAD in the `finally` silently discards the agent's real uncommitted edits along with the mutation, and the subsequent `committed_gate` call sees a clean tree and reports nothing wrong — turning real data loss into an undetected false-clean result. This is latent today only because no spec declares a mutant yet, but the spec explicitly anticipates the next spec doing so.

`_write_file` (the call that actually mutates the tracked file) runs before the `try:` at line 419, so if it raises — which it does whenever the container's `sh -euc 'printf ... | base64 -d > path'` exits non-zero after the shell has already truncated `path` for the redirect — the `finally`'s `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` at lines 421-424 never executes. The exception then propagates straight out of `source_mutated`'s `__enter__`, and `witness_gate` (saffron/gates/core/witness.py lines 143-154, 164-187) sets `applied=False` and reports 'could not apply {file}'s mutant' — exactly the case that same module's own comment on the `Mutated` protocol (lines 78-85) calls out by name as forbidden: 'a raise from `__enter__` must mean nothing was changed... a container exec that applies the edit and then loses the connection is exactly the shape that is not [unreachable]'. The result is a truncated/corrupted worktree file left unrestored while the gate's own message claims nothing was applied — the 'silent dirty tree this gate exists to refuse'. None of the new tests in tests/test_worktree.py exercise a write failure (only read-failure and undo-failure are covered), so this gap is invisible to the suite.

`test_a_failed_undo_raises_rather_than_reporting_a_verdict` claims (comment at line 1128) that "a failure to *apply* raises the same way", but `exploding_exec` only fails the `cat` command (the read half of apply, in `_read_file`); it never fails the `sh -euc ...` write command that `_write_file` (worktree.py:366-382) issues to actually mutate the file. Deleting the `if done.returncode != 0: raise ...` check in `_write_file` (worktree.py:379-382) — so a failed write silently falls through to `yield None` instead of raising `CellRuntimeError` — would keep every test in this diff green, yet violate acceptance criterion 4 ("a failure to apply ... raises rather than reporting a verdict") for exactly the path (`_write_file`) that performs the actual mutation, since no test drives `runtime.exec_` to return non-zero for the `sh` command the way it already does for `cat`.
